Ulyatt & Sons was a well-known London button manufacturer and tailor supplier operating during the 19th and early 20th centuries. They frequently supplied brass and metal buttons for British civil uniforms, railway staff, liveried household staff (butlers, coachmen, footmen), and military/police forces. ​Front Design: Features an ornate interlocking monogram (typically reading stylized letters like "L.W.R." or similar depending on the specific private estate, railway, or institution it belonged to). Livery buttons were custom-cast for wealthy households or corporate entities so that staff uniforms matched the family crest or company insignia. ​Backmark: The back clearly stamps "H. ULYATT & SONS · LONDON", alongside a sturdy self-shank (the loop on the back used for sewing the button onto heavy wool or fabric uniforms).
